rationale: This is the one defensible next step in a heavily mined family — it combines two independently validated structural fixes (scale-consistent SIGN fallback for non-payers, and re-ranking the residual to remove the sign flip from multiplying a negative residual by a positive price rank) rather than tweaking a knob, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis exactly.

target_name: Wide rebalanced residual with graded commitment
rationale: A clean single-element variation of Proposal 1 with a coherent economic reading (dividend commitment intensity beats an integer payer count, whose ties genuinely degrade rank resolution), but it is a measurement refinement of an already-tested purge rather than new economics, so its value hinges entirely on Proposal 1 being run alongside it.

The nested SUMRANK does implement the stated 1/2–1/4–1/4 weighting and blending enterprise with equity multiples has a real rationale (different failure modes for financials and asset-light firms), but choosing the blend weights to match the observed alpha-versus-slope pattern of two prior runs is post-hoc weighting on the same sample and risks manufacturing an average that beats neither leg out of sample.

target_name: Normalized firm yield with rebalanced residual
rationale: Substituting a three-year averaged EBITDA into the price leg is a single, economically motivated knob (management benchmarks against normal earning power) with a sensible complementarity argument against the earnings-volatility purge, but it is close to the boundary of a cosmetic recombination of two already-tested components.

The complementarity argument is not unreasonable, but this is a five-term kitchen sink that fuses the archive's strongest-slope and strongest-alpha financing legs with no way to attribute the result, and the coverage claim is overstated — the marginal leg still requires a full lagged year of both prstkc and dvt, which the SIGN fallback does not restore, so coverage will fall well short of the 0.110 wide-sample level.

target_name: Short window purge for wider coverage
rationale: This is a pure lookback-window tweak with no new economic content, and its stated motivation is internally inconsistent — the binding history requirement in the same expression is TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt,0),5), which still demands five years, so shortening only the volatility window cannot deliver the promised coverage gain toward 0.13.
